home.title: Explore the universe by building it
home.subtitle: Visual tools to understand how planets, stars and galaxies work.

planetLab.title: Planet lab
planetLab.desc: Design a planet and its moon in 3D, tune its physics and find out whether it could host life.

stars.title: Stellar life cycle
stars.desc: From nebula to white dwarf, neutron star or black hole.

orbits.title: Orbital mechanics
orbits.desc: Kepler's laws, Hohmann transfers and Lagrange points.

blackHole.title: Black hole lab
blackHole.desc: Form one from a star, feed it, merge two and watch them bend light.

hints.tidallyLocked: Always shows the same face to its star.

life.title: Probability of life
life.disclaimer: Simplified educational model, not a scientific prediction.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.info: Life's chemistry works best between ~0 °C and ~50 °C.

water.name: Liquid water
water.info: Needs water, plus temperature and pressure that keep it liquid.

atmosphere.name: Atmosphere
atmosphere.info: Suitable pressure and enough gravity to keep the gas from escaping.

size.name: Size
size.info: Very small planets lose their air; very large ones tend to be gaseous.

habitableZone.name: Habitable zone
habitableZone.info: Region around the star where liquid water can exist.

magnetic.name: Magnetosphere
magnetic.info: Shields from radiation and stellar wind. Needs an iron core and rotation.

rotation.name: Rotation
rotation.info: Very long days or tidal locking cause extreme temperature contrasts.

stability.name: Axis stability
stability.info: A massive moon stabilises the tilt, and with it the climate.

star.name: Star type
star.info: Red dwarfs flare violently; F stars are short-lived.

modeHints.form: Create a black hole from a massive star.
modeHints.lab: Tune its parameters and watch it change.
modeHints.feed: Drag across the disk to throw matter at it.

hints.spin: How fast it rotates. Negative: the disk orbits against the hole's spin.
hints.accretion: Fraction of the Eddington limit (maximum stable brightness).
hints.jets: Appear with high spin and moderate accretion.

visitor.tides: Stretching at the horizon (2 m person)
visitor.time: Time dilation at the innermost orbit
visitor.starTorn: would be torn apart {{distance}} from the centre
visitor.starWhole: would be swallowed whole, without breaking up

form.metallicityHint: Heavy elements (Sun ≈ 0.014). More metals → stronger winds and more mass lost.
form.rotationHint: Fraction of break-up speed. Carried over into the black hole's spin.
form.locked: To change the star, start over.

stageText.0: Fuses hydrogen in its core for about {{time}}.
stageText.1: With hydrogen exhausted it swells to ~{{radius}} solar radii and loses mass through winds.
stageText.2: The iron core can no longer release energy and collapses in under a second.
stageText.2wd: The core contracts and the star puffs off its outer layers.

deaths.planetaryNebula: It sheds its layers as a planetary nebula
deaths.fallbackSupernova: Weak supernova: part of the material falls back
deaths.directCollapse: Failed supernova: the whole star collapses
deaths.pulsationalPairInstability: Pair-instability pulses shed mass before the collapse
deaths.pairInstability: Pair-instability supernova: the star is blown apart

remnantText.whiteDwarf: Not massive enough: an Earth-sized white dwarf remains.
remnantText.neutronStar: The core ended up as a neutron star (a pulsar). Try a heavier star.
remnantText.none: The explosion was so violent it left no remnant. Try another mass or higher metallicity.

feed.instructions: Pick an object and drag across the disk plane: where you start is its position and the drag direction its velocity.
feed.exaggerateHint: In reality one star barely changes a big hole's mass. This makes the growth visible.

disrupted.star: Star torn apart by tidal forces
disrupted.planet: Planet torn apart by tidal forces

gasAccreted.gas: The gas cloud is feeding the disk
